items.title: 1 Month With My Homemade Geothermal AC System — Here’s How It’s Doing
items.description: It’s officially been one month since I fired up my homemade DIY geothermal AC system, so it’s time to see how it’s actually performing. Catch up on the video series here. Part 1 - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RhgFEHgjPqY&t=1s Part 2 - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-ee1ZWDiVdQ&t=24s Part 3 - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ntVCKMdNUj0&t=1s Part 4 - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VfJH4ksIz2I&t=156s For this project, I buried roughly 2,000 feet of pipe in the ground and built a closed-loop system designed to use the naturally cooler ground temperature to help cool my house. After weeks of digging, plumbing, wiring, testing, troubleshooting, and making adjustments, I finally got the system running. Now that it’s had a full month of real-world use, I’m checking the water temperatures, airflow, system performance, and overall results to see if this crazy DIY geothermal experiment is actually worth it. In this video I’ll show you how the system has been holding up, what I’ve learned so far, what I would change, and whether I’m still happy with the results. If you haven’t watched Parts 1 and 2 yet, go back and check those out to see how the entire system was built from the ground up. This project is experimental and based on my own DIY setup and experience. Always do your own research and follow applicable electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and building codes. items.title: The Truth About Owning an Outdoor Wood Boiler
items.description: After one full year of heating with an outdoor wood boiler, I’ve learned a LOT — and there are definitely a few things I wish I knew before I started. In this video, I’m sharing 5 of the biggest lessons I learned during my first year of owning and operating a wood boiler. From burning wood and keeping the fire going to maintenance, efficiency, and some of the little things nobody really tells you about, these are the things I think every new or future wood boiler owner should know. Overall, I’ve really enjoyed heating with wood, but there’s definitely more to owning an outdoor wood boiler than just throwing a few logs in the firebox! If you already heat with a wood boiler, let me know in the comments: What’s one thing YOU wish you knew when you first started? And if you’re considering installing one, drop your questions below. I’ll do my best to answer them based on what I’ve learned so far. Thanks for watching! Links to digital temperature controller I used- https://amzn.to/48NCX3U - https://amzn.to/4qaxtYe #WoodBoiler #OutdoorWoodBoiler #WoodHeat #HeatingWithWood #DIY

items.title: I Have a Crazy Heat Pump Idea... Will It Actually Work?
items.description: I've had this idea stuck in my head for a while, and before I start cutting, welding, and building... I want your opinion. Can an old window air conditioner be turned into a DIY water chiller for a hydronic cooling system? The goal is to cool water instead of air and use it with a heat exchanger to cool my house. On paper, it seems possible—but there are a lot of questions. Can the refrigerant system handle it? Would the efficiency be worth it? What problems am I overlooking? In this video, I tear down an old window AC unit, explain the concept, and walk through my plan. Now I'm turning it over to you. 💬 Would this actually work? 💬 What challenges do you see? 💬 Have you ever built something similar? I read the comments, and your feedback often shapes the projects I build next. If enough people think this has potential, there's a good chance you'll see me build it. Catch up on the video series here.
